exposure: increasing predicted risk of cesarean delivery based on a validated prediction model
outcome: maternal morbidity (third-/fourth-degree lacerations, endometritis, blood transfusion, wound infection, venous thromboembolism, hysterectomy, intensive care unit admission, death)
neonatal morbidity (blood transfusion, encephalopathy, intraventricular hemorrhage, severe respiratory distress syndrome, necrotizing enterocolitis, sepsis)
cohort: The study included 8,466 full-term (>=37 weeks) singleton gestations with intact membranes and an unfavorable cervix (Bishop score <=6 and dilation <=2 cm) undergoing induction of labor.
finding: Increasing predicted probability of cesarean was associated with longer labor length and increased maternal and neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: Increasing predicted probability of cesarean delivery was associated with longer labor length and increased maternal and neonatal morbidity.
